subject: ela
intro: Informational books and articles have special features that help you find information. A heading tells you what a section is about. A table of contents shows you where each chapter is. A glossary defines important words. Bold words and captions on pictures also give you information. Knowing how to use these features makes you a better reader.

items.prompt:
A book about ocean animals has a table of contents with these chapters:
Chapter 1: Fish (page 4)
Chapter 2: Sea Mammals (page 12)
Chapter 3: Sea Birds (page 20)

On what page would you find information about dolphins?

steps: I need to find information about dolphins.
Dolphins are sea mammals.
I look at the table of contents for 'Sea Mammals.'
Chapter 2: Sea Mammals starts on page 12.
I would turn to page 12.
solution.answer: I would turn to page 12, because dolphins are sea mammals and Chapter 2 about Sea Mammals starts on page 12.

items.prompt:
A science article has three sections with headings:
'What Frogs Eat'
'Where Frogs Live'
'How Frogs Grow'

Which heading would help you find out what a tadpole is?

steps: I need to find information about tadpoles.
A tadpole is a young frog, so it relates to how frogs grow.
I look for the heading that is about growth.
The heading 'How Frogs Grow' would tell me about tadpoles.
solution.answer: 'How Frogs Grow' would help me find information about tadpoles because tadpoles are a stage in how frogs grow.

items.prompt:
A book has this glossary entry:
habitat (noun): the natural home of an animal or plant.

What does a glossary do for the reader?

steps: I look at what the glossary entry does.
It gives the word 'habitat,' its part of speech, and a definition.
A glossary is a list of important words and their meanings.
The reader can use the glossary to understand unfamiliar words.
solution.answer: A glossary helps the reader by giving definitions of important words in the book. When a reader does not know what 'habitat' means, they can look it up in the glossary.

items.prompt:
An article has a section heading in bold letters that reads: 'How Honeybees Make Honey.' Below the heading, there are four paragraphs.

What does this heading tell the reader?

steps: I read the heading: 'How Honeybees Make Honey.'
Headings tell the reader what the section below is about.
This heading tells me the section will explain the process of making honey.
I can use this heading to quickly find this information.
solution.answer: The heading tells the reader that the section below explains how honeybees make honey. Headings help readers find topics quickly without reading everything.

items.prompt:
An article about weather has a picture of storm clouds. Below the picture is a caption that reads: 'Cumulonimbus clouds can produce thunder and lightning.'

What does a caption do for the reader?

steps: I look at the caption below the picture.
A caption is a label or sentence that explains a photo or illustration.
This caption tells me what kind of clouds are in the picture and what they can do.
Without the caption, I might not know what type of clouds they are.
solution.answer: A caption explains what is shown in a picture. This caption tells the reader that the clouds pictured are cumulonimbus clouds and that they produce thunder and lightning.

items.prompt:
A book called 'All About Seasons' has a table of contents:
Chapter 1: Spring (page 3)
Chapter 2: Summer (page 11)
Chapter 3: Autumn (page 19)
Chapter 4: Winter (page 27)

You want to learn about how animals survive cold temperatures. Which chapter would you go to, and what page does it start?
items.hint: Which season is the coldest? Find that chapter.

steps: Animals survive cold temperatures in winter.
I look for the winter chapter.
Chapter 4: Winter starts on page 27.
I would turn to page 27.
solution.answer: I would go to Chapter 4: Winter, which starts on page 27, because that chapter would have information about surviving cold temperatures.

items.prompt:
An article about plants has these section headings:
'Parts of a Plant'
'What Plants Need to Grow'
'How Plants Make Seeds'

Which heading would help you find out what roots do?
items.hint: Roots are a part of a plant.

steps: I need to find out about roots.
Roots are a part of a plant.
The heading 'Parts of a Plant' would cover what roots are.
I would look under 'Parts of a Plant.'
solution.answer: 'Parts of a Plant' would help me find out what roots do, because roots are one of the parts of a plant.

items.prompt:
A book's glossary has this entry:
pollen (noun): a fine yellow powder made by flowers that helps plants make seeds.

A student is reading and sees the word 'pollen' in the text but does not know what it means. How should the student use the book to find the meaning?
items.hint: Think about which part of the book defines words.

steps: The student needs the meaning of a word.
The glossary is the text feature that gives word definitions.
The student should turn to the glossary and find 'pollen' listed there.
The definition says pollen is a fine yellow powder that helps plants make seeds.
solution.answer: The student should look up the word in the book's glossary, which will give the definition. The glossary entry for 'pollen' says it is a fine yellow powder made by flowers that helps plants make seeds.

items.prompt:
An article about birds has a photo of a penguin. The caption below reads: 'Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 1,500 feet.'

What information does the caption add that the photo alone cannot show?
items.hint: Think about what you can and cannot see in a photo.

steps: A photo shows what a penguin looks like.
It cannot show a number like '1,500 feet.'
The caption adds the fact that penguins can dive very deep.
This is information that requires words, not just a picture.
solution.answer: The caption adds the fact that emperor penguins can dive over 1,500 feet. This is a number and a fact that cannot be shown in a photo alone.

items.prompt:
A nonfiction article has a bold word: The sun is a star, and it is part of the Milky Way galaxy.

The word 'galaxy' is in bold. Why might the author have made it bold?
items.hint: What do bold words usually mean in nonfiction texts?

steps: Bold words in nonfiction often signal important vocabulary.
The author may have made 'galaxy' bold because it is a key word readers need to know.
It signals the reader to pay attention to this word.
It may also mean the word is defined in the glossary.
solution.answer: The author made 'galaxy' bold because it is an important vocabulary word. Bold words signal that a word is a key term readers should pay attention to, and it may be defined in the glossary.
